newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 8.25/8.50 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 8.25/8.50 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 8.25/8.50 percent on Monday on flush liquidity, dealers said.
One local bank dealer said the central bank's early injection of some 1.712 trillion rupiah supplied the market with ample funds.
"The central bank has been keeping the market flush in the past few days. It might be a signal to the market for interest rates easing," the dealer said.

But another dealer said he was unsure about the signal because the central bank raised the seven-day papers (SBIs) rate to 11.75 percent on Monday after lowering it to 11.0 percent from 11.5 percent last Friday.
However, some operators in the dollar-rupiah market were seen converting rupiah funds into dollars in anticipation of narrowing interest rate differentials.
Longer-term rates were also soft, with one- and three-month money seen offered at 13.50 and 14.50 percent, respectively.
The central bank offered overnight SBIs at eight percent to drain some excess liquidity from the market.
It also offered one- to four-day papers at eight percent, 14-day at 12 percent, one-month at 12.75 percent, three-month at 13.75 percent, six- and 12-month at 14.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 9.63 percent, compared with 8.9 percent on Thursday.
